name: Angular

beginner.content:
What is Angular?

• Angular is a TypeScript-based, opinionated front-end framework maintained by Google, used for building large-scale single-page applications (SPAs).
• Unlike React (a library), Angular is a complete framework: it ships with routing, forms, HTTP client, and dependency injection built in.
• Angular apps are built from components - each with a TypeScript class (logic), an HTML template (view), and CSS (style).

Fresher Notes

  • Angular is a TypeScript-based framework from Google for building single-page applications.
  • An app is built from components, templates, services and modules (or standalone components in recent versions).
  • Create a project with ng new my-app and run it with ng serve.

Worked Example 1

Worked Example 2

Practice Exercise 1

Practice Exercise 2

Deep Dive: Internals - How It Works

An Angular app starts in main.ts, which bootstraps the root component. The compiler (Ivy) turns each template into instructions that create and update DOM nodes. When something happens (event, timer, HTTP response) Angular runs change detection from the root: bindings are re-evaluated and only changed DOM parts are updated. Zone.js (or signals in zoneless mode) tells Angular when to check.

Deep Dive: Syntax Options & Variants

Tooling: ng new, ng generate (component, service, pipe, guard), ng build (production bundle with AOT and tree shaking), ng test, ng lint, ng add for schematics. Configuration lives in angular.json and tsconfig; environments and budgets control builds.

expert.content:
Mid-Level Notes

  • The Angular CLI generates code (ng generate component), builds, tests and serves the app.
  • Templates use HTML plus Angular syntax: interpolation {{ }}, property binding [prop], event binding (event).
  • Change detection updates the view when data changes; signals make this more precise in modern Angular.

Senior Notes

  • Choose standalone components over NgModules for new code; they reduce boilerplate and improve tree shaking.
  • Angular is opinionated: dependency injection, RxJS, forms and routing come built in, which suits large teams.
  • Plan for performance: OnPush change detection, lazy-loaded routes, trackBy, and bundle budgets.

Deep Dive: Common Mistakes & Fixes

Beginner mistakes: forgetting to import a standalone component or directive in imports, mutating inputs in children, subscribing without unsubscribing, manipulating the DOM directly instead of using bindings, and putting logic in templates. Let Angular manage the DOM and keep logic in classes.

Deep Dive: Performance & Tuning

Performance basics: production builds (AOT, minification), lazy routes, OnPush, @for with track, avoiding expensive template expressions, image optimization (NgOptimizedImage) and deferrable views (@defer) for below-the-fold content.

Deep Dive: Real-World Scenario

Real-world: a feature-based project structure with lazy-loaded features, a core module of singletons (auth, interceptors), shared presentational components, and strict TypeScript settings for safer refactoring.
codeExamples:
src/app/
  core/       auth.service.ts, auth.guard.ts, auth.interceptor.ts
  shared/     ui/button.component.ts, pipes/money.pipe.ts
  features/
    products/ product-list.component.ts, product-detail.component.ts, products.routes.ts
    orders/   ...
  app.routes.ts, app.config.ts

// OUTPUT:
// each feature builds into its own lazy chunk

beginner.content:
Data Binding

Angular offers 4 kinds of binding between the component class and its template:
1. Interpolation: {{ value }} - display a value.
2. Property Binding: [property]="value" - set a DOM property.
3. Event Binding: (event)="handler()" - respond to DOM events.
4. Two-Way Binding: [(ngModel)]="value" - keep a form input and a property in sync.

Fresher Notes

  • A component combines a TypeScript class, an HTML template and CSS. The @Component decorator declares its selector, template and styles.
  • Data binding connects class and template: interpolation, property binding [x], event binding (x), two-way binding [(ngModel)].
  • Components pass data with @Input() and notify parents with @Output().

Worked Example 1

OnPush component.

Worked Example 2

Cleanup in ngOnDestroy.

Practice Exercise 1

Input and Output.

Practice Exercise 2

New control flow.

Deep Dive: Internals - How It Works

Each component instance has a view. Angular creates it from the template instructions, runs the constructor, sets inputs, calls ngOnChanges and ngOnInit, renders, and during change detection re-checks bindings. When the component is removed, ngOnDestroy runs. Inputs flow down, outputs (events) flow up; this one-directional flow keeps the app predictable.

Deep Dive: Syntax Options & Variants

Modern API: signal inputs (input()), output(), model() for two-way, computed and effect, viewChild, content projection with <ng-content>, host bindings, template reference variables and @ViewChild.

intermediate.content:
Structural Directives - *ngIf and *ngFor

Structural directives change the DOM's structure by adding/removing elements. *ngIf conditionally renders an element; *ngFor repeats an element for each item in a collection.

expert.content:
Mid-Level Notes

  • Control flow in templates: @if, @for, @switch (new syntax) or *ngIf, *ngFor.
  • Lifecycle hooks: ngOnInit, ngOnChanges, ngOnDestroy for setup and cleanup.
  • Use trackBy (or track in @for) so lists update efficiently.

Senior Notes

  • Prefer ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush and immutable inputs for performance.
  • Smart (container) versus presentational components: keep data fetching in containers and display logic in small components.
  • Avoid heavy logic or function calls in templates; use computed values, pipes or signals.

Deep Dive: Common Mistakes & Fixes

Mistakes: mutating arrays or objects passed to OnPush children (no re-render), calling functions in templates (runs every check), using index as track key (wrong DOM reuse), subscribing in ngOnInit without cleanup, and large components that do everything. Use immutable updates, computed values, stable ids and small components.

Deep Dive: Performance & Tuning

Component performance: OnPush, signals, track keys, @defer, virtual scrolling for very long lists (cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport) and avoiding layout thrash. Profile with Angular DevTools to see which components re-render.
codeExamples:
{{ row.name }}
 // OUTPUT: // 100,000 rows rendered with about 20 DOM nodes

expert.content:
Deep Dive: Real-World Scenario

Real-world: a list/detail screen with a smart container that loads data and presentational children that only display and emit events, so the children are reusable and easy to test.

beginner.content:
Services & Dependency Injection (DI)

A Service is a plain TypeScript class that holds logic/data meant to be shared across components (e.g. an API client). Angular's DI system automatically creates and supplies (injects) a service instance to any component that asks for it in its constructor - you never call new yourself.

Fresher Notes

  • A service is a class that holds logic or data shared between components, such as HTTP calls.
  • Mark it with @Injectable({ providedIn: "root" }) and ask for it in a constructor or with inject().
  • Dependency injection (DI) creates and supplies the instance for you.

Worked Example 1

Fake service in a test.

Worked Example 2

Error handling with retry.

Practice Exercise 1

A data service.

Practice Exercise 2

An auth interceptor.

Deep Dive: Internals - How It Works

Angular's injector tree resolves dependencies by type token. When a class asks for a service, the injector looks in the element/component injector, then up through parents to the root, creating the instance on first use and caching it per injector. providedIn: 'root' makes a tree-shakable singleton; component-level providers create an instance per component.

Deep Dive: Syntax Options & Variants

Provider options: useClass, useValue, useFactory, useExisting, InjectionToken for configuration, multi providers (interceptors), and inject() in functions. HttpClient returns cold Observables; operators (map, switchMap, retry, shareReplay) shape the stream.

expert.content:
Mid-Level Notes

  • HttpClient returns Observables; subscribe or use the async pipe in templates.
  • Provide services at root (singleton), at component level (one per component tree) or in route providers.
  • Use interceptors for cross-cutting concerns: auth headers, error handling, logging.

Senior Notes

  • Keep components thin: put data access and business rules in services and test them in isolation.
  • Use injection tokens and interfaces to swap implementations (for example fake API in tests).
  • Avoid manual subscriptions in services; return Observables and let components use the async pipe or takeUntilDestroyed.

Deep Dive: Common Mistakes & Fixes

Mistakes: unsubscribed Observables, nested subscribes (use switchMap), services holding component state in public mutable fields, circular dependencies, and swallowing HTTP errors. Return Observables, use the async pipe and a central error strategy.

Deep Dive: Performance & Tuning

HTTP performance: cache read-mostly responses, cancel stale requests with switchMap, batch calls, enable compression and HTTP caching headers on the server, and avoid refetching on every navigation.

Deep Dive: Real-World Scenario

Real-world: a token refresh interceptor. On 401 it obtains a new token once (shared among concurrent requests) and retries the failed requests.

beginner.content:
Angular Router

The Angular Router maps URL paths to components, enabling navigation within a single-page app without a full page reload. Routes are declared as an array of path → component mappings.

Fresher Notes

  • The Angular router maps URLs to components. Routes are an array of objects: { path: "products", component: ProductListComponent }.
  • Put <router-outlet> in a template where the routed component should appear, and link with routerLink.
  • Route parameters (:id) are read with ActivatedRoute or the withComponentInputBinding option.

Worked Example 1

Functional guard.

Worked Example 2

Programmatic navigation.

Practice Exercise 1

Route configuration with lazy loading and a guard.

Practice Exercise 2

Reading parameters.

Deep Dive: Internals - How It Works

The router parses the URL into a tree, matches it against the route configuration (first match wins), runs guards and resolvers, loads lazy chunks, creates or reuses components, and renders them into the matching router-outlet. Navigation is a pipeline of events (NavigationStart, GuardsCheck, ResolveEnd, NavigationEnd) that you can observe.

Deep Dive: Syntax Options & Variants

Options: withComponentInputBinding (route data as inputs), withPreloading(PreloadAllModules), withInMemoryScrolling, route data and title, nested children with multiple outlets, canMatch to choose routes by condition, and runGuardsAndResolvers.

intermediate.content:
Route Parameters

Dynamic segments in a route path (e.g. :id) let one route template handle many URLs, with the actual value read via ActivatedRoute.

expert.content:
Mid-Level Notes

  • Features: child routes, redirects, wildcard 404 route, lazy loading with loadComponent/loadChildren, guards and resolvers.
  • Query parameters carry optional state (filters, page) and keep URLs shareable.
  • Use Router.navigate for programmatic navigation.

Senior Notes

  • Lazy load feature routes to keep the initial bundle small, and preload important ones.
  • Guards (canActivate, canMatch) protect routes; remember the server must enforce authorization too.
  • Use resolvers or signals to load data before showing a screen, and handle loading and error states explicitly.

Deep Dive: Common Mistakes & Fixes

Mistakes: wrong route order (a wildcard before specific routes), forgetting pathMatch: 'full' on empty-path redirects, relying on client guards for security, memory leaks from unsubscribed route observables, and losing state on navigation. Order routes from specific to general and enforce authorization on the server.

Deep Dive: Performance & Tuning

Routing performance: lazy load feature areas, preload what users will need next, keep resolvers fast, and cache data in services so back navigation is instant. Check chunk sizes with the build stats.

Deep Dive: Real-World Scenario

Real-world: an admin area guarded by a role check, lazy loaded, with a "leave without saving?" guard on edit screens.

cheatNotes: @Component - Decorator that marks a class as an Angular component
Interpolation {{ }} - Display a component property's value in the template
[property] - Property binding, sets a DOM element property
(event) - Event binding, calls a method on a DOM event
[(ngModel)] - Two-way binding between a form input and a property
*ngIf - Structural directive, conditionally renders an element
*ngFor - Structural directive, repeats an element per collection item
@Injectable - Marks a class as available for dependency injection
providedIn: root - Registers a service as a singleton for the whole app
Constructor injection - Angular supplies service instances via the constructor
RouterModule - Enables client-side routing between components
routerLink - Directive for SPA navigation without full page reload
router-outlet - Placeholder where the routed component renders
ActivatedRoute - Service to read route parameters and query params
Module (@NgModule) - Groups related components, directives, and services
Pipe - Transforms displayed values in a template, e.g. {{ date | date }}
Lifecycle hooks - ngOnInit(), ngOnDestroy(), etc. run at specific component stages
RxJS Observable - Stream of async values used throughout Angular (HTTP, forms, router)
HttpClient - Angular's built-in service for making HTTP requests
Standalone components - Components that don't require an NgModule (modern Angular)
